title: Bournemouth Come From Behind to Beat Celta Vigo and Keep the Run Alive
body:
Bournemouth recovered from a deficit to beat Celta Vigo 2-1 [S1].

Sky Sports framed the result around European history, saying the win created two bits of history [S1]. BBC Sport focused on the streak, reporting a ninth successive win under new manager Marco Rose, with Evanilson again central to the story [S2]. A run that long stops looking like a lucky patch and starts looking like an identity.

The form backs that up. Across their last five league matches they have won all five, collecting 15 points, scoring 11 and conceding just one [ST1]. A side that leaks almost nothing while scoring freely is hard to bet against, and the defensive record deserves as much credit as the goals.

That is the sort of afternoon that changes the mood around a dressing room. There is no hiding from a scoreline, and this one will be picked apart all week, but the pressure now sits with the next opponent to find a way to stop this momentum.

The Touchline Take: file this one under unfinished business, because a run this sharp has not yet peaked.
